newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end up,boosted by buying of medium-term bonds.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end up,boosted by buying of medium-term bonds.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended higher on Monday due to buying of medium-term bonds and the yen's surge against the dollar.
"The medium-term sector was extraordinarily strong today, with demand for (the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd's) bank debentures leading the way," a foreign bank trader said.

There was talk that an agricultural financial institution and a long-term credit bank received medium-term fixed interest rates, and this also contributed to the firmness of medium-term bonds, traders said.
The September ended at 123.20, up sharply from Friday's close of 122.84. Turnover was 35,810 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.470 percent as of 0622 GMT, down from Friday's close of 2.495 percent.
The yield of the 190th JGB, which is expected to take over the benchmark mantle from the 182nd within the week, stood at 2.595 percent, down from Friday's close of 2.615 percent.

Market players may have been buying IBJ's May five-year bank debentures with a coupon rate of 2.2 percent based on speculation, which proved true, that the IBJ may cut the coupon rate for its new June debentures to two percent, some said.
The IBJ said on Monday it would cut its long-term prime rate for June to 2.9 percent from 3.1 percent in May, effective on Wednesday.
The long-term credit bank also said it would set the coupon rate for its June five-year bank debentures at two percent, down from 2.2 percent in May.
Buy backs of bank debentures have been conspicuous since about two weeks ago, the foreign bank trader said.
"The spread between bank debentures and (five-year) JGBs stood at 30 basis points at one point, but has decreased since, causing traders who had sold earlier to buy back," he said.

In morning trade, JGBs rose due to dealers' short-covering which was triggered by the release of weak U.S. jobs data over the weekend, which eased fears of a possible near-term credit-tightening in the United States.
The dollar's fall to as low as 111.80 yen around midday in Tokyo, also supported JGBs, traders said.

"It was not so much the dollar's fall below 112 yen which triggered buying of JGBs. The simple fact that the yen was on a rising trend against the dollar was considered a buy factor," a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
The dollar was quoted at 112.75/85 yen as of 0652 GMT.
Five-year IRS rates were quoted at 2.16/20 percent as of 0653 GMT, down from about 2.20/24 percent on Friday.
The decline of medium-term IRS rates encouraged strong bids for medium-term JGBs, the trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
The IBJ's May five-year bank debentures with a coupon rate of 2.2 percent were traded at 2.02 percent on Monday.
The Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd are due to announce their prime rates and terms for June debentures on Tuesday.
-- Masayuki Kitano, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-5473-3748
